title.value: Workflow Discovery from Dialogues in the Low Data Regime
title.justification: This title is obtained directly from the introductory details and the main focus of the paper, which discusses discovering workflows from dialogues.
title.quote: Workflow Discovery from Dialogues in the Low Data Regime Amine El Hattami

extractions.description: The paper introduces 'Workflow Discovery' (WD) as a new task focused on extracting workflows from text-based dialogues. The aim is to identify actions from dialogues without pre-existing formal documentation, enhancing automated dialogue systems. The approach utilizes sequence-to-sequence models to discover workflows and improve few-shot and zero-shot learning in unseen domains. The paper tests its approach on the Action-Based Conversations Dataset (ABCD) and MultiWOZ, achieving state-of-the-art results in related tasks.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme of the paper is on discovering and optimizing workflows from dialogues to improve task-oriented dialogue systems. While this has various applications in efficiency and automation, it is not directly focused on climate or ecological sustainability.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Text-based dialogues are now widely used to solve real-world problems. In cases where solution strategies are already known, they can sometimes be codified into workflows.

primary_category.justification: The paper is focused on natural language processing and dialogue systems, with no direct relevance to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_category.quote: We propose a novel task we call Workflow Discovery (WD) to extract the actual workflow followed by an agent from a task-oriented dialogue.

secondary_categories.justification: No secondary categories related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development are discussed in the paper, as its primary focus is on dialogue and workflow extraction.
secondary_categories.quote: Our contributions can be summarized as follows: • We propose a new formulation to the problem of workflow extraction from dialogues, which, to our knowledge, has not been examined or framed as we present here.

primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-categories relevant to ecological or climate sustainability are not addressed in this paper.
primary_sub_category.quote: Our approach is targeted toward the task of analyzing chat transcripts between real people, extracting workflows from transcripts, and using the extracted workflows to help design automated dialogue systems.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The sub-categories relevant to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development are not applicable here.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Our WD problem formulation here is related to dialogue act modeling in the sense that different steps along our workflows may be composed of dialogue acts.

applications.justification: The paper discusses the application of extracting workflows from dialogues to automate and optimize dialogue systems, enhancing efficacy in task-oriented dialogues.
applications.quote: Our approach is targeted toward the task of analyzing chat transcripts between real people, extracting workflows from transcripts, and using the extracted workflows to help design automated dialogue systems or to guide systems that are already operational.

new_primary_category.justification: The existing categories are sufficient, and the paper doesn't introduce a new avenue related to sustainable development beyond technological efficiency in dialogues.
new_primary_category.quote: We propose a new formulation to the problem of workflow extraction from dialogues.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: As this is focused on NLP and dialogue systems, it does not necessitate a new sub-category within ecological or climate context.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: The WD task is defined as follows: Workflow Discovery (WD) to extract the actual workflow followed by an agent from a task-oriented dialogue.
